title: Add incremental attribution checking with checkpoint records
summary: Extend `athena check --attribution` so a pass writes a checkpoint record to athena/records, later runs judge only commits and records after the newest checkpoint, and `--full-replay` ignores checkpoints and fails on disagreement. CI runs incremental on push and full replay on schedule; each run reports seconds, commits and records judged; measured timings go in CHANGELOG. Audience: maintainers and CI.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for incremental, tampered checkpoint, version change; clippy clean.
Criteria check judged counts and failures, not existence.
One focused change in the attribution check, CLI and CI.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Full replay is a flag on `athena check --attribution` (e.g. `--full-replay`).

Only the CI push run (and explicit invocation) writes checkpoints; the writing uses the existing records-branch writer in athena-gate/athena-data, and a failed push of the checkpoint does not fail the check.
Checkpoint verifier_version is a constant derived from the check's version (e.g. crate version plus a rule revision); changing it forces replay.
The record-count judged is the landings and intents read on the records tip beyond the checkpoint's records tip.
Timings are measured by running the built binary locally; no governance config beyond ci.yml changes.

acceptance_criteria.text: Test run: `cargo test` passes, including a test where an incremental run after a checkpoint judges only the commits added since it (the judged count equals the number of new commits, less than a full replay's).
Test run: a test with a tampered checkpoint (naming a main commit the full replay fails) shows the full replay reports a finding and exits non-zero because it disagrees with the newest checkpoint.
Test run: a test shows a checkpoint with a different verifier_version (check version) forces a full replay, judging everything from the start.
Test run: after a passing check a checkpoint record is written to athena/records with main sha, records tip sha judged against, and check version; a failing check writes none. Tests cover both.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
Each run's output (text and --json) reports seconds taken, number of commits judged and number of records judged.
.github/workflows/ci.yml attribution job runs incrementally on push and as a full replay on the schedule event.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry with the full-replay time and the incremental time (one landing behind) on this repository, each marked measured, taken from actual runs.
The --help text for check documents the incremental and full-replay modes.

out_of_scope: Changing the legacy rule or pr-head check
Changing the Checkpoint record schema unless strictly needed
departures: Larger than typical: new git-writing path, CLI, CI and measurement work across several crates.
